titleStmt.title: Draft Note to the South African Prime Minister and Minister for External Affairs

head.hi: Draft Note to the South African Prime Minister and Minister for External Affairs

div.p: Excellency: I have the honor to refer to the efforts which my Government is making to promote a revival of international commerce by means of reciprocal trade agreements authorized by the Trade Agreements Act of June 12, 1934. Such agreements have been concluded with a number of European and Latin American countries and negotiations with a considerably larger number of countries are in various stages of progress. Eventually it is hoped to conclude trade agreements with all the important commercial countries.

In accordance with the established policy of my Government to accord most-favored-nation treatment to all countries which accord such treatment to American commerce, concessions granted under trade agreements are extended to all countries which treat American commerce no less favorably than they treat the commerce of any other foreign country. The procedure which has been adopted for the purpose of carrying out the provisions of the Trade Agreements Act in respect of the generalization of concessions was explained in a mimeographed press release of April 1, 1935, a copy of which is enclosed with this note. There is enclosed also a copy of the President’s letter of October 7, 1935, in regard to the application of the customs duties proclaimed in connection with the trade agreements with Belgium, Haiti, and Sweden.

As a result of this policy of generalizing concessions, the Union of South Africa has been listed among the countries which enjoy the minimum tariff rates imposed in the United States. As the trade agreements program of the United States advances, the Union of
South Africa may benefit importantly from the extension of trade agreement concessions to its commerce. It is not unlikely that the tariff rates on a number of products of considerable importance to the Union will be reduced in connection with trade agreements now pending or contemplated.

Later on, after trade agreement negotiations now in progress and others in regard to which tentative plans have been made have been concluded, my Government is desirous of exploring the possibility of entering into negotiations looking toward the conclusion of a trade agreement, involving reciprocal tariff concessions, with the Union of South Africa.

Having in mind the possibility of trade agreement negotiations at some favorable time in the future, my Government has instructed me to propose to your Government that a simple agreement providing for reciprocal most-favored-nation treatment be entered into at an early date, with a view to stabilizing commercial relations between the United States and the Union of South Africa pending the conclusion of a mutually satisfactory trade agreement.
My Government would greatly appreciate an early response to this proposal.

note.p: For text of agreement signed February 27, 1935, see Department of State Executive Agreement Series No. 75 or 49 Stat. 3680.
For text of agreement signed May 25, 1935, see Department of State Executive Agreement Series No. 79 or 49 Stat. 3755.
This note was presented to the South African Prime Minister on January 25, 1936, and was acknowledged by him on February 4, 1936 (611.48A31/42). No further reply was received.
